definitions.explanation: Completely black without any other color; extremely dark.
Having darkened significantly from sun exposure.
Colloquial: obviously guilty or corrupt (opposite of 'innocent').

examples.japanese: {空|そら}が{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}な{雲|くも}に{覆|おお}われた。
examples.english: The sky was covered with pitch-black clouds.

examples.japanese: {焦|こ}がしてしまって、{鍋|なべ}の{底|そこ}が{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}になった。
examples.english: I burned it, and the bottom of the pot turned pitch black.

examples.japanese: {日焼|ひや}けで{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}だ。
examples.english: I'm really tanned from the sun.

examples.japanese: {夏休|なつやす}みで{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}に{日焼|ひや}けした。
examples.english: I got really tanned over summer vacation.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}で{遊|あそ}びすぎて、{子供|こども}たちは{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}に{焼|や}けて{帰|かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: The children played too much at the beach and came home deeply tanned.

examples.japanese: あいつは{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}だ。
あの{政治家|せいじか}は{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: That politician is said to be totally corrupt.

examples.japanese: {証拠|しょうこ}が{次々|つぎつぎ}と{出|で}てきて、{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}は{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}だとわかった。
examples.english: As evidence kept coming out one after another, it became clear the suspect was totally guilty.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{真|ま}っ (emphatic prefix) + {黒|くろ} (black)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}に{焦|こ}げる - to burn black
・{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}な{夜空|よぞら} - pitch-black night sky
・{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}の{髪|かみ} - jet-black hair

COLLOQUIAL USAGE:
In colloquial Japanese, {真|ま}っ{黒|くろ} (innocent: {白|しろ}) is used to describe someone clearly guilty or corrupt, like the English "guilty as sin."

RELATED:
・{真|ま}っ{白|しろ} - pure white
・{真|ま}っ{暗|くら} - pitch dark
